nameStory: This moss gets its "smooth-stalk" name from the sleek, unbranched stems that hold up its spore capsules - quite different from its rough-stalked cousin! The "feather-moss" part comes from how its delicate, overlapping leaves create a soft, feathery texture that looks almost like tiny green plumes.
description: Smooth-stalk Feather-moss is a common carpet-forming moss that creates soft, yellowish-green to bright green mats on various surfaces. It grows in loose, spreading patches rather than tight cushions, with stems that can reach 2-4 inches long. The individual plants have a delicate, feathery appearance thanks to their small, overlapping leaves that curve gracefully along the stems. This adaptable moss is found worldwide and can even grow under artificial lighting in places like caves.

idTips.label: Growth Form
idTips.description: Forms loose, spreading mats rather than dense cushions, with stems that trail and branch irregularly across surfaces

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Tiny leaves overlap like shingles and curve slightly, creating a soft, feathery texture that feels silky when you gently brush it with your finger

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Ranges from yellowish-green when dry to bright, vibrant green when moist - the color change is quite dramatic after rain

idTips.label: Sporophytes
idTips.description: Spore capsules sit atop smooth, reddish-brown stalks (setae) that feel firm and unbranched when gently touched

idTips.label: Texture
idTips.description: Feels soft and slightly springy underfoot, with a silky smoothness when stroked - not coarse or bristly like some mosses

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Extremely adaptable, growing on soil, rocks, logs, and even concrete - often in areas with some disturbance

habitat: This adaptable moss thrives in a wide variety of New England habitats, from forest floors and rotting logs to rock walls and even urban concrete surfaces. It's particularly common in areas with some human disturbance like trail edges, old foundations, and disturbed soil. You'll find it from sea level to moderate elevations, often mixed with other common mosses in partly shaded to fully shaded locations.

seasonality.spring: Becomes vibrant green as moisture increases, with new growth appearing bright and fresh. Sporophyte capsules may be developing on their smooth stalks.
seasonality.summer: May appear more yellowish-green during dry periods but quickly greens up after rain showers. Active growing season with best development of characteristic feathery texture.
seasonality.fall: Often produces mature spore capsules on their distinctive smooth stalks. Color remains green in moist conditions but may fade during dry spells.
seasonality.winter: Remains visible under snow cover, often appearing more compressed but still identifiable by its soft texture and growth pattern when exposed.

funFact: This moss is so adaptable to artificial lighting that it actually thrives in Wisconsin's Crystal Cave, using only electric lights to photosynthesize in complete absence of natural sunlight - making it one of nature's first "indoor gardeners"!
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with its close relative, Rough-stalked Feather-moss, but you can tell them apart by gently feeling the spore-bearing stalks - smooth and sleek in this species versus rough and textured in its cousin. Remember: "Smooth name, smooth stalk!"
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called a "feather-moss," this isn't related to feathers at all - the name simply describes the delicate, plume-like appearance of the leafy stems. The scientific name "salebrosum" means "rough" or "uneven," which seems contradictory to its smooth stalks but actually refers to the irregular, bumpy way it grows across surfaces.
compareHints: Among its Brachythecium relatives, Smooth-stalk Feather-moss is the most generalist - while Waterside Feather Moss prefers wet areas and Whitish Feather-moss has a distinctly paler color, this species grows almost anywhere. Its smooth spore stalks are the key difference from Rough-stalked Feather-moss, and it lacks the distinctive pleated leaves of Pleated Foxtail Moss.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Unlike its relatives Smooth-stalk and Rough-stalked Feather-moss which can tolerate drier conditions, Waterside Feather Moss is strictly aquatic in its needs.

Among its feather-moss relatives, Rough-stalked Feather-moss stands out for its bumpy stem texture — Smooth-stalk Feather-moss feels smooth, Waterside Feather-moss prefers wet areas, and Whitish Feather-moss has a distinctly paler, more silvery appearance.
Compared to its Brachythecium relatives like Rough-stalked and Smooth-stalk Feather-moss, Whitish Feather-moss is distinctly paler in color and typically smaller in overall size.

Unlike its relatives Waterside Feather Moss (which prefers wet areas) and Smooth-stalk Feather-moss (which forms denser mats), Pleated Foxtail Moss has those distinctive pleated leaves and prefers drier, more disturbed habitats.
